raw_response:
I have farmed this land in Quzhou for over forty years. My father farmed it before me. I know what grows here and what doesn't.

The soil is sandy loam, the water table is dropping, and the summers are hot and dry. Every farmer around me does wheat-maize rotation, and I do the same. I have about thirteen mu total — twelve in the main fields and one small plot near the house for vegetables.

For the wheat, I already put it in the ground last October, so that crop is underway. But I still need to plan my inputs for the coming months — the jointing and heading irrigations, the topdressing nitrogen, the herbicide spraying. I use the improved wheat seed from the county seed station, same variety as my neighbor Old Li. I apply more nitrogen than the technicians from the agricultural bureau say I should — they say twelve or fifteen jin, I use eighteen. In my experience, less fertilizer means less grain, and I cannot afford a poor harvest.

After wheat comes off in June, I will immediately plant summer maize on the same twelve mu. I always buy Zhengdan 958 hybrid seeds from the township market. I rotary-till lightly and seed the same day or the next day. Summer has rain, so I only irrigate once, unless July turns dry.

The one-mu vegetable plot I manage for the household and to sell a little at the village market. Mixed vegetables — cabbage, beans, some peppers. My wife handles most of this, but I do the heavy ploughing and the irrigation.

I am sixty years old. I will not experiment. I will farm the way that has fed my family.
